pr_title: Fix editor settings still displayed when replaced
pr_body:
- Fixes #94577

Even though no consensus was achieved about what to do with removed or replaced settings in the editor settings, I suggest this PR to fix the problem where old settings `run/output/always_open_output_on_play` and `run/output/always_close_output_on_stop` are displayed in the editor settings if the user migrates from an earlier version of Godot.

This PR adds the `EditorSettings::_remove_deprecated_settings` method and calls it when loading editor settings. It's the easiest way to fix the problem and can be used for future removal or replacement of editor settings.
pr_comments: There might be more settings that need to be erased.

comments:
This option does not exist anymore after the PR [#91033](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/91033)

The new option is `Action on stop` in `Run > Bottom Panel`.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5aceaf0c-aef8-4309-8b7e-f6621d02d8a0)

In this PR, I originally created a conversion to copy the old setting to the new, but I was asked to remove it. The problem with the Godot settings is that settings that are removed are still present in the setting window if they were modified.

 I could create a new PR for the setting conversion to prevent a lot of questions from users migrating from 4.2 to 4.3.

This is probably a very naive questions from someone who's not really familiar with the codebase but: Why are we displaying properties that are not linked to anything in the code?

Wouldn't the simple solution be to discard all unknown properties?

The problem arises from the fact that plugins can create settings, and they can do so not only at startup. Therefore, removing settings that are not from Godot would also remove settings from plugins. There is a proposal about this: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4444
